# mnemos-mesh Operations Runbook

> Audience: on-call operator running `mnemos-mesh` in production.
> Scope: cert rotation, peer add/remove, common failures, metrics, logging.
> Companion: `docs/en/admin/security.md` covers the mTLS threat model;
> this runbook covers day-2 operations.

## Quick reference

| Task | Command | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Health check | `mnemos-mesh doctor --config /path/to/mesh.yaml` | Exit 0 = healthy |
| Cert rotation | `kill -HUP $(pidof mnemos-mesh)` | No stream drop |
| Build | `make build` | Static binary, ~13MB |
| Verify (CI gates) | `make verify` | Tests + lint + coverage floor |
| Scrape metrics | `curl http://localhost:9090/metrics` | Prometheus format |

## Doctor command — `mnemos-mesh doctor`

`doctor` is the operational health probe. Run it before `serve`, on
`ExecStartPre`, on a cron, or after any change to `mesh.yaml`.

```bash
mnemos-mesh doctor --config /etc/mnemos/mesh.yaml
```

### Checks performed

| # | Check | What it verifies | Fails doctor? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | config schema | `cfg.Validate()` — node_id, listen, socket parent dir, mTLS file existence, fingerprint format, peer address syntax, metrics listen | Yes |
| 2 | mTLS material | pins parse, certs/CA load, node cert not expired | Yes |
| 3 | Unix socket | `net.DialTimeout("unix", cfg.UnixSocket)` — mnemos is listening | Yes |
| 4 | peer reachability | TCP dial each peer's address; ALL peers failing fails doctor, single failure is reported only | Yes if all peers fail |

### Output format

```
✅ config (node_id=node-a, peers=3)
✅ mtls (certs loadable, node cert valid)
✅ unix_socket (/run/mnemos/core.sock reachable)
  peer node-b (mesh-b.example:8443): reachable
  peer node-c (mesh-c.example:8443): reachable
✅ peers (2/2 reachable)
doctor: OK
```

A `⚠️` line (not a failure) means the node cert expires within 7 days
— rotate soon. A `❌` line is a failed check; doctor exits non-zero.

### Flags

| Flag | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `--config PATH` | `~/.mnemos/mesh.yaml` | Path to mesh.yaml |
| `--peer-timeout DURATION` | `2s` | Per-peer TCP dial timeout |

## Cert rotation (SIGHUP)

The mesh reloads cert material on `SIGHUP` **without dropping active
Subscribe streams**. New connections see the new cert; existing
connections keep their negotiated session until they close naturally.

### Procedure

1. Replace the cert/key/CA files on disk at the paths in `mesh.yaml`
   (`mtls.ca_cert`, `mtls.node_cert`, `mtls.node_key`).
2. Send SIGHUP:

   ```bash
   kill -HUP $(pidof mnemos-mesh)
   ```

3. Watch the log for the outcome:

   - Success: `cert rotation triggered (SIGHUP)` → `cert rotation complete; new connections use new cert, existing connections drain`
   - Failure: `cert rotation failed; serving previous cert` — old cert preserved; fix files and SIGHUP again.

### Why SIGHUP, not restart

A restart drops every active Subscribe stream; each peer then has to
reconnect and replay from its last cursor. SIGHUP avoids that —
the cert swap is atomic (via `atomic.Pointer` in `internal/mtls/rotation.go`),
and `GetCertificate` is called per new handshake, so only new
connections see the new material.

### Rotation cadence

Default `mtls.rotation_days: 90`. The mesh does not auto-rotate — the
operator (or a cron job) must replace the cert files and SIGHUP. Use
`doctor` after rotation to confirm the new cert is within its validity
window.

## Peer add / remove

Peers live in the `peers:` list of `mesh.yaml`. Adding or removing a
peer requires a config reload — there is no live peer registry today.

### Add a peer

1. Generate the peer's cert (signed by the same private CA).
2. Compute its fingerprint:

   ```bash
   openssl x509 -in peer.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha256 | \
     sed 's/.*=//; s/://g; s/^/sha256:/'
   ```

3. Add to `mesh.yaml`:

   ```yaml
   peers:
     - id: node-d
       address: mesh-d.example:8443
       fingerprint: "sha256:<hex>"
       projects: ["project-x"]
   ```

4. Add the same fingerprint to `mtls.peer_fingerprints` keyed by `id`:

   ```yaml
   mtls:
     peer_fingerprints:
       node-d: "sha256:<hex>"
   ```

5. SIGHUP the mesh (cert reload also reloads the pinned-fingerprint
   set — they share the reloader).

   ```bash
   kill -HUP $(pidof mnemos-mesh)
   ```

6. Run `doctor` to confirm the new peer is reachable.

### Remove a peer

1. Delete the peer entry from `peers:` and the matching
   `mtls.peer_fingerprints` key.
2. SIGHUP.
3. Active streams from that peer will be rejected on their next
   handshake attempt (their fingerprint is no longer pinned).

## Common failures

### mTLS handshake failures

Symptom: `mnemos_mesh_mtls_handshake_failures_total{peer_id="..."}` rising
in Prometheus; log line `mtls: peer ... fingerprint mismatch` or
`mtls: peer chain invalid`.

| Cause | Diagnostic | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Peer cert expired | `doctor` warns/expired; `openssl x509 -in peer.pem -noout -enddate` | Reissue peer cert, rotate peer side, SIGHUP both |
| Peer cert not signed by the private CA | `mtls: peer chain invalid` in log | Reissue cert from the same CA |
| Fingerprint pin mismatch (wrong cert rotated) | `fingerprint mismatch (pinned X, got Y)` | Update `peer_fingerprints` to the new cert's fingerprint |
| Unknown peer connecting (attack or wrong config) | `peer ... not in pinned set` | Confirm the peer's `id` matches its cert CN; reject if unexpected |

### Unreachable peer

Symptom: `doctor` reports `❌ peer ...: dial timeout` or `connection refused`;
`mnemos_mesh_rpc_total{...status="error"}` rising for that peer's RPCs.

| Cause | Fix |
|---|---|
| Peer mesh process down | SSH to peer host, `systemctl status mnemos-mesh`, restart |
| Firewall blocking the port | Open TCP on the peer's `listen` port |
| DNS resolution failure | Check `/etc/hosts` or DNS; verify `address` syntax |
| Peer rotated its cert and forgot to update pin | Update `peer_fingerprints`, SIGHUP |

A single unreachable peer does **not** fail `doctor` (the mesh is
still partially functional). All peers failing fails `doctor`.

### Cursor lag

Symptom: `mnemos_mesh_cursor_lag{peer_id="..."}` is non-zero and growing.

| Cause | Fix |
|---|---|
| Slow peer (CPU/network bound) | Scale the peer host; check its `mnemos-mesh` log for backpressure |
| Stalled Subscribe stream (network blip) | Peer will reconnect with its last cursor; if it does not, restart the peer's mesh |
| mnemos source side not emitting events | Check mnemos's own logs; the mesh only relays what mnemos returns |

### Config validation failure

Symptom: `serve` or `doctor` exits with `config: schema validation failed:
N problem(s): ...`.

| Common field error | Fix |
|---|---|
| `node_id: must not contain whitespace` | Remove spaces/tabs from `node_id` |
| `unix_socket: parent dir ...: no such file` | `mkdir -p $(dirname cfg.UnixSocket)` (the mesh does not create the parent) |
| `mtls.ca_cert: ...: no such file` | Confirm path; check perms |
| `mtls.peer_fingerprints[X]: must be "sha256:"<hex>` | Reformat to `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` |
| `peers[N].id: "X" duplicates peers[M].id` | Peer ids must be unique |
| `metrics.listen: ... is not a valid host:port` | Use `host:port` or `:9090` |

## Metrics reference

The mesh exposes a Prometheus scrape endpoint at `metrics.listen`
(default `:9090`). Override at runtime with `--metrics-addr`.

```bash
curl http://localhost:9090/metrics
```

### Metric catalogue

| Metric | Type | Labels | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mnemos_mesh_peer_count` | gauge | (none) | Active peer connections (post-mTLS handshake) |
| `mnemos_mesh_rpc_duration_seconds` | histogram | `rpc`, `peer_id` | FederationPeer RPC latency in seconds |
| `mnemos_mesh_cursor_lag` | gauge | `peer_id` | Subscription cursor lag (events behind local head) |
| `mnemos_mesh_mtls_handshake_failures_total` | counter | `peer_id` | Total mTLS handshake failures |
| `mnemos_mesh_rpc_total` | counter | `rpc`, `peer_id`, `status` | Total FederationPeer RPCs by terminal status |

### Label cardinality

All labels are bounded:

- `rpc` ∈ `{Pull, SyncMetadata, Subscribe, Heartbeat}` — fixed set.
- `peer_id` — bounded by the configured peer registry (a few dozen at most).
- `status` ∈ `{ok, error}` — fixed set.

No free-form strings are emitted as labels.

### Suggested alerts

| Alert | Expression | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| mTLS handshake failures | `rate(mnemos_mesh_mtls_handshake_failures_total[5m]) > 0` | warning |
| High RPC error rate | `rate(mnemos_mesh_rpc_total{status="error"}[5m]) / rate(mnemos_mesh_rpc_total[5m]) > 0.1` | warning |
| Sustained cursor lag | `mnemos_mesh_cursor_lag > 100` for 10m | warning |
| No active peers | `mnemos_mesh_peer_count == 0` for 5m | critical |
| RPC latency p99 high | `histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(mnemos_mesh_rpc_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) > 1` | warning |

### Why a separate listener

The metrics listener is on a separate port from the gRPC peer listener
so it can be firewalled off from peers and exposed only to the
scraper. The gRPC port carries mTLS; the metrics port is plain HTTP
(assume the scraper is on a trusted network or behind a reverse proxy
with auth).

## Logging reference

The mesh emits structured logs (JSON or text) to stdout via
`slog`. Configure in `mesh.yaml`:

```yaml
logging:
  level: info   # debug | info | warn | error
  format: json  # json | text
```

### Key log fields

| Field | Where | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `node_id` | serve startup | This node's peer id |
| `listen` | serve startup | gRPC peer listener address |
| `metrics_addr` | serve startup | Prometheus scrape listener address |
| `peer_id` | per-RPC | The peer that initiated the RPC |
| `rpc` | per-RPC | `Pull` / `SyncMetadata` / `Subscribe` |
| `latency_ms` | per-RPC | Handler wall-clock latency |
| `trigger_code` | per-RPC | `EXHAUSTIVE` (M5.1 — only value today) |
| `err` | on error | Wrapped error |

### Useful log lines

| Event | Message |
|---|---|
| Start | `mnemos-mesh starting` |
| Peer listener up | `peer listener ready` |
| Metrics listener up | `metrics listener ready` |
| Cert rotation start | `cert rotation triggered (SIGHUP)` |
| Cert rotation done | `cert rotation complete; new connections use new cert, existing connections drain` |
| Cert rotation failed | `cert rotation failed; serving previous cert` |
| Shutdown | `shutdown signal received` → `shutdown complete` |

### Log level guidance

- `debug` — per-record Subscribe sends; only for development.
- `info` (default) — startup, per-RPC summary, rotation events.
- `warn` — degraded state (mnemos dial failed, send failures).
- `error` — cert rotation failure, metrics listener bind failure.
